overview: The MPS School Committee oversees the Medford Public Schools, managing district-wide policy, budgeting, and facility planning. Over the span from early 2024 through late 2026, the committee focused on significant capital infrastructure projects, including a multi-year effort to rebuild Medford High School and the electrification of elementary and middle school HVAC systems. The body navigated a transition in executive leadership, ultimately appointing a permanent superintendent from within the district. Current work centers on developing a new district strategic plan, managing elementary school overcrowding, and finalizing schematic designs for school renovations.

threads.name: Medford High School Building Project
threads.summary: The committee initiated a multi-year partnership with the MSBA to replace or renovate Medford High School, beginning with the appointment of a building committee and completion of the eligibility phase. Work moved into a feasibility study that evaluated site options, ultimately narrowing choices after discovering a 1967 deed restriction on Edgley Field. The committee approved a comprehensive educational plan to guide design, which includes vocational program expansion and student support facilities. Most recently, the project entered the schematic design phase with updated membership and cost estimates.

threads.name: Superintendent Leadership and Evaluation
threads.summary: After a multi-year tenure, Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent departed the district in early 2025. The committee appointed Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi as interim leader to ensure continuity during major facility and budget cycles. Following a year of transitional leadership and positive performance evaluations, the committee voted to appoint Dr. Galusi as the permanent superintendent. Formal contracts and a realigned evaluation cadence were established to match the academic year.

threads.name: District Budgeting and Supplemental Funding
threads.summary: The committee managed several complex budget cycles, including the transition of ARPA-funded positions to the general operating fund. In late 2024, voters approved local tax overrides, leading to a supplemental budget that restored literacy coaches, behavioral specialists, and custodial staff. The committee also established a special education reserve fund to manage unanticipated costs. Recent joint meetings with the City Council have focused on closing multi-million dollar gaps required to maintain level services.

threads.name: Elementary School Overcrowding and Space Planning
threads.summary: Severe overcrowding at Roberts Elementary School prompted the committee to explore redistricting and grade reconfiguration. Immediate measures included relocating preschool classrooms to Missituk Elementary and hiring additional staff at the Roberts school. The committee studied a potential shift to K-4 and 5-8 grade spans across the district but eventually voted to delay implementation until 2028 to allow for better financial planning. Current work focuses on a formal policy to regulate intra-district enrollment and reassignment requests.

threads.name: Middle School HVAC Replacement
threads.summary: The district addressed failing HVAC systems at the Andrews and McGlynn middle schools through a phased $25 million infrastructure project. The committee authorized a construction management at risk approach and a major bond request to fund the transition from obsolete refrigerants to modern cooling systems. The project included roof refurbishments and was designed to restore classroom cooling. By late 2026, the committee reallocated remaining capital funds as the project neared completion.

threads.name: Vocational Program (CTE) Expansion and Admissions
threads.summary: The committee worked to expand Career and Technical Education (CTE) offerings, including plans for a new plumbing program. To manage high demand and waitlists, the body adopted a lottery-based admissions policy that shifted away from weighted criteria to ensure equitable access. Recent initiatives include the introduction of an honors pilot program for juniors and seniors. The committee also updated viability forms for the MSBA to reflect current enrollment trends and student retention pathways.

threads.name: Transportation Logistics and Bus Safety
threads.summary: Transportation issues were a recurring challenge due to regional bus driver shortages that led to route cancellations and overcrowding. The committee developed student surveys to assess needs and implemented a tiered bus monitoring system using paraprofessionals to improve safety. A five-year contract with Eastern Bus was approved, including a feasibility study for future fleet electrification. Recently, the district introduced late bus service for the high school to increase student access to extracurricular activities.

threads.name: Policy Modernization and Student Rights
threads.summary: The committee updated various policies to align with state and federal mandates, including comprehensive Title IX grievance protocols and a district water wellness policy. New guidelines were established for the ethical use of generative artificial intelligence, prohibiting its use by educators for qualitative grading. The body also passed resolutions affirming support for LGBTQIA+ students, menstrual equity, and protections for students affected by Temporary Protected Status terminations.
